subject.title: feat: per-job elevated exec scoping for cron and heartbeat

question: Should OpenClaw solve elevated cron and heartbeat authority as narrow per-job/heartbeat approval markers, or fold it into the broader non-forgeable scheduling and heartbeat provenance model?
rationale: The answer changes the host-elevated exec trust boundary across persisted cron jobs, agent-created schedules, HEARTBEAT.md/config edits, synthetic providers, audit records, and upgrade behavior, so automation should not choose the permanent model.

options.title: Fold Into Provenance Design
options.body: Treat this issue as the elevated-exec requirement for the broader scheduling provenance work while explicitly keeping heartbeat provenance and migration in scope.

options.title: Implement Narrow Markers
options.body: Add per-job elevated approval state plus heartbeat modifier provenance now, with create/update/execution checks and upgrade tests.

options.title: Fail Closed Internals
options.body: Remove wildcard internal-source elevation for cron-event and heartbeat unless maintainers define an explicit compatibility path.

recommendation.title: Fold Into Provenance Design
recommendation.body: Treat this issue as the elevated-exec requirement for the broader scheduling provenance work while explicitly keeping heartbeat provenance and migration in scope.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent merged cron caller-scope work makes this the closest current owner path for scheduling provenance decisions.
